The low's 'leaving painting, writing and invention to others' shares its frame with closed (Big Five)'s 'leaving ideas to others'.

set_notes.Big Five: One shape across the ten: a single sentence of 29 to 32 words running the domain's facets as a comma list, six clauses for O, A and N, five plus a two-part gloss for C, five or six for E. Seven of the ten open with a gloss and a colon (open, closed, conscientious, careless, extraverted, introverted, emotionally-stable), three are a bare list (agreeable, antagonistic, neurotic): same grain, not quite the same shape, and the agreeable pair and neurotic are the ones a re-edit would give an opening phrase. Six facets in 31 words is denser than the corpus examples (three or four clauses), so each facet gets four or five words and the lists edge toward the catalogue the writer's brief asked to avoid; that is the price of six facets in 32 words and Roger may accept it. Provenance is uneven across poles: the high poles stand on the chapter's definitions, facets, markers and item examples; the low poles of A and C stand largely on PAR's average-range sample-client sentences sharpened to vice level (disclosed in the notes); O and E on the sample's low and very-low text; emotionally-stable is derived. Phrase reuse inside the set: 'in company' and 'under stress' (neurotic, emotionally-stable), 'inherited' (open, closed).
set_notes.HEXACO: One shape across the twelve: a single sentence of 29 to 32 words, four clauses, one per facet, from hexaco.org's one sentence per pole, no gloss anywhere (tough has five clauses, dependence twice; emotional's fourth clause is two-part). Within the set the grain is even. Against the Big Five set the difference is systematic: four facets in the same word budget gives each clause seven or eight words and a concrete image (desk, calendar, painting, landscape, shoulder) where a Big Five clause has four or five, so the two instruments' descriptions differ in texture as well as content; expected, since the sources differ the same way. Sharpening is uneven: the vice poles are tightened past hexaco.org's hedges (quarrelsome, careless, sly, conventional), the virtue poles stay at source level, and tough, not a vice pole, is tightened too (entry issue). Phrase reuse that follows the theory (HEXACO H took sincerity and modesty from Big Five A): 'dealing straight' (honest-humble, agreeable (Big Five)); 'flattering ... to get what one wants' (sly, antagonistic (Big Five)); plus 'shrugging' (introverted, and closed (Big Five)) and 'leaving ... to others' (conventional, and closed (Big Five)). Nearest-existing lines are sound throughout; honest-humble and sly are rightly called the new axis; agreeable (HEXACO) names the ad-hoc agreeable and the difference without the words 'near-duplicate', which matches the queue (it carries no near_duplicate tag).

summary:
22 drafts checked against their recorded passages and the corpus form: all 22 pass form (one sentence, 29-32 words, 'This means' opening, no hedges, instrument and partner unnamed, US spelling, inside voice); 19 ok, 3 edit, all 22 nearest-existing lines plausible.
The three: antagonistic (Big Five) 'boasting' has no low-side source (suggested swap to 'putting oneself first', or add the facet list to its record and keep it); closed (Big Five) 'paying feelings no mind' has no low-side source and the note's 'five of six' is four (a record fix, the description can stand); tough (HEXACO) 'walking toward physical danger without a second thought' turns 'not deterred' into recklessness (suggested 'pressing on where one could get hurt').
Pairs: I agree with all eleven of the writer's pair reviews and add a scope gap in conscientious/careless (Big Five) (the low drops achievement and competence its own source supplies), the fear-versus-approach mismatch in emotional/tough, the weak anxiety inversion and one absence-shaped clause in neurotic/stable, and mirror phrasing in open/closed and the HEXACO C pair.
Set: Big Five drafts are six-clause lists at four or five words a facet, seven of ten with a gloss; HEXACO drafts are four-clause lists at seven or eight words a facet, none with a gloss; even within each set, different texture between the two, following the sources.
